# Stellar validation v4: eclipsing binaries, rotation and transients

## Eclipsing binaries

Reference: Prša et al. 2022, ApJS 258, 16 (TESS Eclipsing Binary stars I, sectors 1-26), VizieR J/ApJS/258/16; the 2-Gaussian model columns (Dp-2g, Wp-2g, Phip-2g, Ds-2g, Ws-2g, Phis-2g), the period and the morphology coefficient (Matijevič et al. 2012: 0 widest detached, 1 ellipsoidal).

- Held out (24 EBs): flagged 17 of 24 = 0.71 (95% CI 0.51-0.85); period within 0.5% 17 of 24 = 0.71 (95% CI 0.51-0.85); aliases: 0 at half, 0 at double the catalogue period.
- Primary depth, ours/catalogue: 0.97 (95% CI 0.95 to 1.10), n = 17.
- Secondary phase within 0.01: 14 of 15 = 0.93 (95% CI 0.70-0.99); a secondary found at all: 15 of 15 = 1.00 (95% CI 0.80-1.00).
- Width rank correlation (Spearman, 17 pairs): 0.96. Morphology (detached or not) agrees: 15 of 17 = 0.88 (95% CI 0.66-0.97).
- Tuning split (6 EBs, not counted): flagged 5 of 6 = 0.83 (95% CI 0.44-0.97); period 5 of 6 = 0.83 (95% CI 0.44-0.97).
- Contrast set: 1 of 7 planet hosts and quiet stars flagged: pi Men not flagged; WASP-126 not flagged; HD 15337 not flagged; TOI-270 not flagged; TOI-236 flagged; zeta Tuc not flagged; beta Hyi not flagged.
- Injected detached EBs: period within 0.5% 60 of 70 = 0.86 (95% CI 0.76-0.92); flagged 70 of 70 = 1.00 (95% CI 0.95-1.00).

## Rotation

Reference: Canto Martins et al. 2020, ApJS 250, 20 (rotation periods of TESS objects of interest), VizieR J/ApJS/250/20, table 1 (unambiguous rotation periods). A single TESS sector is about 27 days with a gap in the middle, and SPOC PDC removes some long-term variability, so periods longer than about 13 days are not measured from one sector; the module reports them as beyond its limit. Stitching sectors needs care with sector-to-sector offsets and is not validated here.

- Held out (24 stars): detected 20 of 24 = 0.83 (95% CI 0.64-0.93); within 10% 14 of 24 = 0.58 (95% CI 0.39-0.76); within 10% of the period, half or double 17 of 24 = 0.71 (95% CI 0.51-0.85); uncertainty covers the difference (2σ) 14 of 14 = 1.00 (95% CI 0.78-1.00).
- Ours/published among detections: 1.05 (95% CI 1.02 to 1.07), n = 20.
- Tuning split (6 stars, not counted): within 10% 4 of 6 = 0.67 (95% CI 0.30-0.90).
- Quiet stars: 0 of 3 with a detected period.
- Injected spot modulation (1-12 d): within 10% 58 of 60 = 0.97 (95% CI 0.89-0.99); 2 at half or double. Beyond the limit (13-30 d, reported only): 11 of 15 reported as beyond it, 3 reported as a period (an alias inside the range).

Reference: Fausnaugh et al. 2023, ApJ 956, 108 (four years of type Ia supernovae observed by TESS), VizieR J/ApJ/956/108, table 1 (peak TESS magnitude, time of peak) and table 3 (time of first light, rise time). Table 3's BJD column is BJD - 2457000 (the ReadMe says 2470000; the values are in the TESS range).

- Held out (15 supernovae): a candidate within 10 d of the published peak 14 of 15 = 0.93 (95% CI 0.70-0.99) (not marked as a likely false alarm: 13 of 15 = 0.87 (95% CI 0.62-0.96)); peak within 2 d 9 of 15 = 0.60 (95% CI 0.36-0.80).
- Rise time ours/theirs (10 with a first-light fit): 0.76 (95% CI 0.55 to 1.06), n = 10. Peak magnitude ours minus theirs: 0.56 (95% CI -0.20 to 0.85), n = 14.
- Class hint extragalactic-transient-like among detections: 7 of 14 = 0.50 (95% CI 0.27-0.73).
- Control apertures (30): with an extragalactic-like candidate 0.23; with any candidate 0.67.
- Tuning split (5 supernovae, not counted): detected 5 of 5 = 1.00 (95% CI 0.57-1.00); peak within 2 d 3 of 5 = 0.60 (95% CI 0.23-0.88).
- Proxima Cen S11-12: 98 candidates match one of Medina et al.'s 134 flares; flare-like 68 of 98 = 0.69 (95% CI 0.60-0.78); classes {'asteroid-crossing-like': 1, 'flare-like': 68, 'momentum-dump-like': 3, 'unclassified': 26}. AU Mic S1 (tuning): {'asteroid-crossing-like': 3, 'flare-like': 40, 'momentum-dump-like': 1, 'periodic-variability-like': 4, 'unclassified': 17}.
- Quiet stars: 46 candidates not marked as false alarms in 83.6 days (0.550 per day).
- Injected false alarms: marked 45 of 60 = 0.75 (95% CI 0.63-0.84) (momentum dumps 25 of 30 = 0.83 (95% CI 0.66-0.93); asteroid-like bumps 20 of 30 = 0.67 (95% CI 0.49-0.81)); found at all 54 of 60 = 0.90 (95% CI 0.80-0.95).

## Not validated

- Planet vetting: unchanged. The eclipsing-binary module's vetting hints are advisory, no vetting decision uses them, and they were not evaluated; using them in vetting needs its own pre-registered evaluation.
- Eclipse widths: Prša et al. (2022) give 2-Gaussian widths, SetuHQ a full width at half depth, so only their rank order is compared. The e·cosω values are first-order hints from the secondary's phase, not compared with radial-velocity orbits.
- Rotation: one sector per star, as the protocol fixes; periods longer than about 13 days are not measured, and stitching sectors (with care for sector-to-sector offsets) is not done and not validated. Canto Martins et al. (2020) used every sector available to them.
- Transients: one TESScut sector per supernova, as the protocol fixes. When first light falls before that sector begins, the reference image already holds supernova light, so the rise time and the peak brightness are measured from a non-zero floor; the supernovae compared are all type Ia, so the extragalactic class hint is not tested on tidal disruption events or other transients.
- Scattered light: no labelled real sample was found; the screen (quality flags and control apertures) is described and exercised on synthetic events and the supernova cutouts' control apertures, not validated against a catalogue of scattered-light events.
- Asteroid crossings: screened by shape and, in cutouts, by a moving centroid; no catalogue of TESS asteroid crossings was compared (Fausnaugh et al. 2023's asteroid flags excluded those supernovae from the sample).

## Data and credit

Public TESS data from MAST: SPOC 2-minute light curves (Jenkins et al. 2016) and TESScut cutouts of SPOC full-frame images (Brasseur et al. 2019). TESS is funded by NASA's Science Mission Directorate. Published values: Prša et al. 2022 (ApJS 258, 16), Canto Martins et al. 2020 (ApJS 250, 20), Fausnaugh et al. 2023 (ApJ 956, 108) and Medina et al. 2020 (ApJ 905, 107), through VizieR (CDS, Strasbourg). No CHEOPS data are used.

- An eclipsing binary or a transient SetuHQ finds is a candidate, never new and never confirmed.
- Morphology and transient classes are heuristic hints from the light curve alone.
